title: Experimental Realization and Phase-Space Winding of a Topological Defect State in the Quantum Rabi Model
authors: Kyungmin Lee, Jiyong Kang, Sunkyu Yu, Jaehun You, Wonhyeong Choi, Taehyun Kim
abstract: We experimentally realize a topological defect state of the quantum Rabi model in a single trapped $^{171}\mathrm{Yb}^{+}$ ion. The state is supported by a tunable interface arising from the oscillator's intrinsic number-dependent coupling in the Fock-state-lattice representation. We independently prepare the state at each sideband-phase setting and reconstruct its motional phase-space distribution using characteristic-function tomography. The resulting Wigner-centroid trajectories exhibit winding numbers of one and zero in the two coupling regimes. Changing the carrier amplitude rescales the trajectories while preserving their windings. Carrier-amplitude modulation provides a complementary dynamical probe, yielding a spin response consistent with the excitation gaps and accessible transition channels from the defect state. The experiment connects topological defect-state physics in a nonuniform synthetic lattice to the measurable phase-space geometry of a hybrid spin-boson system.
summary: This research experimentally realizes and probes the topological defect state in the Quantum Rabi Model using a single trapped ion. By reconstructing the motional phase-space distribution, the authors measured the winding number of the Wigner-centroid trajectory, confirming its topological nature based on coupling parameters. This connects abstract topological physics to measurable quantum dynamics in trapped-ion systems.
main_problem: The paper aims to experimentally realize and characterize the phase-space winding of a topological defect state within the Quantum Rabi Model (QRM).
main_result: The experiment successfully measured phase-space winding numbers of one and zero, confirming the predicted topological invariant based on the relative strengths of coupling parameters ($g_1$ vs $g_2$).
method: The authors used characteristic-function tomography to reconstruct the motional phase-space distribution and analyzed the winding number of the Wigner-centroid trajectory.
model_or_system: The physical system is a single trapped $^{171}	ext{Yb}^+$ ion, which is used to realize the QRM. The system is mapped onto a Fock-state lattice, and the defect state arises from a tunable interface created by number-dependent couplings.
key_observables: Wigner-centroid trajectories, winding numbers ($W$), and spin response ($\Delta_0$) measured via carrier-amplitude modulation.
important_parameters: Coupling ratios ($g_1/g_2$), carrier amplitude modulation depth ($\delta w_a$), and sideband phase settings ($\phi_1, \phi_2$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the validity of the Fock-state lattice representation and the ability to accurately reconstruct the motional state via tomography.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the QRM in an FSL, compare measured vs. simulated characteristic functions, and show reconstructed Wigner functions demonstrating the winding number dependence on coupling regimes.
paper_structure: The paper details the Hamiltonian formulation, describes the experimental measurement techniques (tomography, modulation), presents the key results showing the winding number dependence, and concludes by connecting the findings to the underlying topological physics.
why_interesting: This work provides a direct, measurable link between abstract topological invariants (winding numbers) and the measurable phase-space geometry of a hybrid spin-boson system realized with trapped ions.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Quantum Rabi model in a trapped-ion Fock-state lattice. (a) A three-tone Raman drive couples the internal spin and one motional mode of a single 171Yb+ ion. The carrier sets w, while the red- and blue-sideband tones set g1eiϕ1 and g2eiϕ2 in Eq. (1). (b) Spin–Fock-state lattice generated by these couplings. The upper and lower rows show the regimes g2 > g1 and g1 > g2, respectively. Black vertical links denote the carrier coupling. Red and blue diagonal links denote the two sideband couplings, whose strengths increase with Fock number. Green markers indicate the calculated defect-state population on the |↑⟩or |↓⟩spin sublattice in the respective regimes.

FIG. 2. Characteristic-function tomography for g1 > g2, rc = 2, rs = 0.25, ϕ1 = −π/3, and ϕ2 = 0. Columns show the real and imaginary parts of X(β). Rows show experiment (Exp.) and the ideal-state calculation (Sim.) from Eq. (2). The conditional motional-state fidelity inferred from their overlap is 0.915 ± 0.013.

FIG. 3. Measured phase-space winding for ϕ2 = 0 and rs = 0.25. Open and filled circles show fitted Wigner cen- troids for rc = 1 and 2. Dashed and solid curves are the cor- responding predictions of Eq. (3). Red trajectories (g1 > g2) enclose the origin once, while blue trajectories (g1 < g2) do not. Arrows indicate increasing ϕ1. Insets show selected re- constructed Wigner functions with fitted centroids marked by black dots and the predicted trajectories overlaid.

FIG. 4. Carrier-modulation response of the defect state for g1 > g2, rc = 1, rs = 0.25, and ϕ1,2 = 0. (a) Energy differences |En,± −E0|/h as the Stark shift increases to its experimental value. Blue solid and red dashed curves identify n = 1, and gray curves show higher doublets. (b),(c) Measured and simulated RMS spin response ∆0 versus modulation depth and frequency. The simulation includes the Stark shift and motional heating. Horizontal lines mark the n = 1 gaps at the endpoint of (a). Gray ticks mark higher gaps as spectral references, not additional direct carrier transitions from the defect state. All panels share the frequency scale.

FIG. 5. Simulated defect-state preparation fidelity for (a) wtarget = gmax and (b) wtarget = 2gmax, versus ramp time and ϕ1, at ϕ2 = 0 and gtarget min /gmax = 0.25. Linear and sinusoidal ramps follow Eq. (B5). Dashed lines mark the inverse ideal- gap scale 229.5 µs. The simulations include the drive-induced Stark shift with maximum magnitude |δS|/(2π) ≃2.23 kHz during the ramp and motional heating calibrated to a ground- state rate of 6 quanta/s.
